findings.F1: The Calmar fails because one fall dominates: the chained daily book returns a yearly 35.2 % against a deepest fall of 58.5 %, which took 271 days to reach its trough across w1 to w3 while holding the coins fell 62.4 % over the same days; the next four falls (30 to 38 %) also came while holding fell 30 to 79 %.
findings.F2: The book is mostly a long position in the coins, not timing: of its mean daily return of 0.112 %, 0.071 % is the market's own rise (mean allocation 0.60), so it rides the coins' falls with them.
findings.F3: The book loses its falls on coin-days when the coin is below its 60-day average price: in the two lowest quintiles of distance to that average the book still held 0.24 and 0.43 of its value and lost 0.39 % and 0.32 % per coin-day, against +0.19 % and +1.27 % per day in the two highest quintiles (allocation 0.84 and 0.87).
findings.F4: Only the largest surges carry a move: cases whose 24-hour return exceeds 1.88 times its 30-day mean absolute value earn +1.97 % above the 5-day drift (t 3.23, 455 cases), while the four lower quintiles earn between -0.54 % and +0.17 % (455 to 454 cases each); the forecast is capped at twice the usual move and so sizes these surges no larger than ones that carry nothing.
findings.F5: Measured over all its cases, the idea's unusual move is +0.12 % per case against a round-trip cost of 0.19 % (0.6 times the cost), whereas the top-surge quintile's +1.97 % is about 10 times the cost.
findings.F6: The 7-day-return regime does not select the move: cases in the lowest 7-day quintile (0 to 0.9 %) earn +0.03 % and the middle three quintiles -0.16 % to -0.31 %; only the top quintile (above 12 %) earns +1.58 % (t 2.06), and 16 % of its cases lose more than 10 %.
findings.F7: Below the 60-day average, ordinary surges lose and only the largest pay: by tercile of surge size, cases below that average earn -0.61 %, -0.67 % and +1.01 % (t 1.79), and cases above it earn -0.35 %, +0.72 % and +0.98 % (376 to 415 cases per cell).
findings.F8: A rising month helps: cases by 30-day-return quintile earn -0.37 %, -0.24 %, +0.27 %, +1.16 % (t 1.96, 361 cases) and +0.53 %.

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, first reaches several times its 30-day average absolute daily return on the upside, the price keeps rising over the next 5 days by more than the coin's usual 5-day return, only while its price is above its 60-day average price. The larger that 24-hour return against its 30-day average absolute daily return, the larger the rise, and the rise keeps growing for surges well beyond twice the usual daily move.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys exceptional up surges only in coins trading above their 60-day average, sizes larger for the largest ones, and stays out of surges in coins below that average, where the book took its deepest falls.
ideas.name: surge continuation above 60-day average

ideas.idea: When a coin's 24-hour return, read at an hourly close, first reaches several times its 30-day average absolute daily return on the upside, the price keeps rising over the next 5 days by more than the coin's usual 5-day return, only while its 30-day return is positive. The larger that 24-hour return against its 30-day average absolute daily return, the larger the rise, with most of it after surges of twice the usual daily move and more.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys the largest up surges in a coin rising over the month and refuses surges in a coin falling over the month, which the 7-day rise does not screen out.
ideas.name: surge continuation in rising month
